blocuri.text: Treasury accounts have a property no other account in bookkeeping has: they can be checked against a reality outside the firm. The balance of the bank account in the books must equal what the bank statement says — a figure issued by someone else, which cannot be adjusted.

That is why treasury is, at the same time, the simplest part of bookkeeping and the best error detector in the whole firm. Simple, because the operations are few and obvious. A good detector, because any mistake shows up immediately, by comparison.
The four accounts and the difference between them

randuri: 5121 Bank accounts in lei
the current account balance — checkable against the statement
5124 Bank accounts in foreign currency
the same, for each currency separately
5311 Cash in lei
cash on hand, checkable against the cash register
5314 Cash in foreign currency
cash in foreign currency, kept separately
blocuri.nota: Foreign currency is kept in two currencies at once: in its own currency and in lei, at the exchange rate on the date of the transaction. The exchange-rate difference is adjusted at closing — chapter 26.

blocuri.text: The practical difference between bank and cash isn't the size of the amounts, but verifiability. The statement comes from the bank, so it's external evidence. You draw up the cash register yourself, so no external evidence exists — the only possible check is actually counting the cash in the drawer.
Collection and payment: two simple entries
Treasury operations are, in their overwhelming majority, simple entries: a cash/bank account and a third-party account.

randuri: The customer paid the invoice
5121 Bank
4111 Customers
the money came in, the receivable was extinguished
We paid the supplier
401 Suppliers
5121 Bank
the liability was extinguished, the money went out
blocuri.nota: Notice that neither entry involves any revenue or expense account.

blocuri.text: Payment is not an expense, and collection is not revenue. They extinguish liabilities and receivables that arose earlier, with another document.

This is the same idea the book started with, in chapter 1: earnings and money are different things. Here it takes accounting form. The expense was recorded when the invoice arrived; the payment only extinguishes the debt. Whoever records the expense both at the invoice and at the payment counts it twice — the classic mistake of firms that work "from the bank statement".
The cash balance cannot be negative
It's the only statement in bookkeeping that anyone can verify, with no training at all: you cannot take more money out of a drawer than you put into it.

A negative cash balance is not a treasury problem, but a recording error — every time, without exception. The causes are almost always two: a collection that wasn't recorded, or a payment recorded with a date earlier than the actual one.

It deserves to be treated as an alarm, not an inconvenience. Software that calmly displays "−1,240 lei" in the cash register is actually hiding a missing document — and that document is also missing from VAT and from the result.
The internal transfer trap

When you move money from the bank to the cash register, or the other way around, you have an operation that appears twice: once as an outflow from the bank, on the statement, and once as an inflow into cash, in the cash register. The two documents often arrive separately, and if each is recorded on its own, the amount gets doubled.

That's what account 581 Internal transfers is for, a transit account: the outflow from the bank credits it, the inflow into cash debits it, and at the end its balance must be zero. If it isn't zero, one end of the transfer is missing.

It's a good example of an account that doesn't represent anything in the real world — there is no safe called "internal transfers". It exists only to make visible a movement that could otherwise get lost between two documents.

The cash register is drawn up daily, for every day with transactions, and the balance is carried forward from one day to the next — it is not accumulated monthly; its form and rules are those set out in the regulations on financial-accounting documents. For foreign-currency treasury, records are kept simultaneously in the foreign currency and in lei, at the exchange rate on the date of the transaction, and at each closing the balances are revalued at the rate published by the BNR for the last banking day of the period; the differences go to financial revenue or expense, not adjusting the cost of the original transactions. Account 581 must be checked at every closing: a nonzero balance signals either an unrecorded end of a transfer, or a movement actually in transit at the closing date — and the two are distinguished only by looking at the documents, not the figure. Finally, a credit balance on a bank account is not an error, but an overdraft, which is presented in the balance sheet as a short-term financial liability, not as negative cash on hand; confusing this legitimate case with a negative cash balance, which is always an error, is the source of unnecessary corrections.
What comes next

The money is recorded. What remains is the part that gives treasury its true value: reconciliation against the statement, i.e. the only check in bookkeeping that relies on evidence coming from outside the firm.
That is the next chapter, and it is the best error-finding tool in the whole book.

enunt: The cash register for day 14 shows: opening balance 800 lei, collections 2,400, payments 3,900, closing balance −700 lei.
(a) What certainly happened? (b) What do you look for, in what order?
rezolvare: (a) Nothing "happened" — you cannot take out of a drawer money that isn't there. A negative cash balance is ALWAYS a recording error, never a real situation.
(b) First hypothesis: a missing collection. Compare the receipts issued that day against what was recorded — at least 700 lei collected is missing.
Second: a payment dated incorrectly, belonging to another day. Check the payment documents from the 14th against those from neighboring days.
Third, rarer: a bank deposit recorded only on the cash side, without its counterpart on the statement — in which case account 581 will show a balance, which is the second free check.
What should NOT be done: "adjusting" the balance with a balancing figure. That hides the missing document, and that document is also missing from VAT and from the result.

blocuri.text: The cash register: the required form

The cashier's office has its own register, with a prescribed form, and its rigor comes from a simple fact: it's the only patrimony element that can be counted at any time and for which no external evidence exists.

randuri: drawn up DAILY, for each day with transactions
the balance must be checkable against the cash on hand, on any day
the balance is carried forward from the previous day
otherwise the day has no starting point
it is not accumulated monthly
a monthly total cannot be checked against anything
it is numbered continuously
a gap means a day with no record
blocuri.nota: All four follow from the same requirement: the count at the end of the day must give exactly what the register shows.

blocuri.text: Hence an organizational consequence: the cashier's office belongs to the firm, not to the person. The money in the drawer is not the cashier's, and mixing it with personal money — even temporarily, even with the intention of putting it back — makes the balance impossible to check and turns an administrative operation into a matter of liability.
What is checked automatically, every month
Treasury is the area where most checks can be done without anyone's intervention, because they are all calculated from data already recorded. Software can run them continuously.

randuri: the cash balance is not negative, on any day
a missing collection or a wrongly dated payment
the cash balance ceiling at the end of the day
exceeding Law 70/2015
payment and collection ceilings, per day and per partner
splitting, even if the documents look correct
the balance of account 581 is zero at closing
an unrecorded end of an internal transfer
the statement balance = the book balance, after reconciliation
any transaction missing from either side
blocuri.nota: The first four are calculated from your own records. The fifth is the only one that requires an outside source — and that's why it's the strongest.

blocuri.text: It's worth noting that four out of five need no new document: they are questions asked of existing data. This is the typical case where automation doesn't save time, but catches something a person wouldn't check every day — and ceilings are usually exceeded on ordinary days, not on the days when someone is keeping an eye on them.

puncte: Treasury is the only part of bookkeeping checkable against external evidence: the bank statement.
Payment is not an expense and collection is not revenue — they extinguish liabilities and receivables that arose earlier.
Whoever records the expense both at the invoice and at the payment counts it twice.
A negative cash balance is always a recording error, never a real situation.
Movements between bank and cash pass through 581 Internal transfers, whose balance must be zero at closing.
A credit balance at the bank is something else: it's an overdraft, i.e. a liability — not an error.
